definition: Abjure means to reject or renounce something formally and publicly.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abjure. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abjure should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: As a condition of joining the neutral mapmakers' guild, the navigator had to abjure, in writing and before witnesses, her allegiance to the crown that had trained her.
Refuse is the everyday no — you can refuse seconds at dinner without a second thought; abjure is a renunciation made formally and in public.
Renounce is milder only in its setting: you can renounce a habit privately, while abjure adds the ceremony — witnesses, a record, sometimes an oath.

To recant is to take back a statement or belief you once voiced publicly, usually under pressure. Abjure is broader and more ceremonial: you can abjure a tie you never put into words, swearing it away formally before witnesses. Recant undoes your own past words; abjure casts the thing itself off.

To disavow is to deny that something is yours — a statement, a policy, a follower's actions — refusing responsibility or connection. Abjure goes further: it is a sworn, public renunciation made on the record. Disavowing pushes a thing away by denying it; abjuring formally gives it up before witnesses.
